title: Eliminate legacy route aliases and normalize flag encoding across runtime and admin APIs
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Background: Over the past three years we accumulated multiple routing aliases and a legacy flag transport layer that encodes rollout/version metadata in query params and ad-hoc headers (v0). These aliases complicate routing, cause duplicated telemetry, and prevent reliable canonicalization of rollout manifests. This ticket removes the alias endpoints and migrates runtime and admin surfaces to a single canonical flag encoding (manifest JSON) while preserving customer-facing compatibility during a short migration window.
acceptance_criteria: All legacy route aliases (/_r/*, /v0/flags/*, /legacy-route-redirects) are removed from the gateway config and runtime no longer accepts alias Host/Path pairs
Runtime and admin APIs accept and emit a single canonical flags manifest JSON schema (manifest_v2) and reject v0 query-param transports with a deprecation warning header
Compatibility shim removed from the public gateway; internal compatibility adapter kept behind runtime feature-flag for 2 sprints then removed
No customer 5xx errors reported during canary rollout; token-level telemetry shows <0.1% increase in latency and <0.01% increase in error rate attributable to this change
SDKs and Console have been updated to stop generating v0-style requests; docs updated and migration guide published
tasks: Inventory: generate complete map of active aliases using logs and routing table (eng-observability query)
Design: finalize manifest_v2 schema and canonicalization rules (link to design doc)
Implementation: add server-side manifest_v2 decoder and strict validation in admin service
Compatibility shim: implement transparent adapter that maps v0->manifest_v2 and logs deprecation events (behind feature-flag)
Gateway config: remove alias routes and add explicit 410 responses for removed paths with migration instructions
SDK updates: patch JS/Python SDKs to emit manifest_v2 and include telemetry for any legacy usage
Migration scripts: backfill persisted flag states from legacy DB columns to canonical store
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring and escalation plan
Cleanup: remove compatibility adapter and feature-flag launch code after successful rollout
migration_plan: Step 1: Run inventory job to identify active customers using legacy routes and contact them via automated email and Console banner. Step 2: Deploy compatibility adapter behind feature-flag in staging and enable for a small internal fleet for 48h. Step 3: Release gateway change that returns a deprecation header for v0 requests and link to migration guide. Step 4: Canary the removal of alias routes according to canary rollout percentages with pre-defined SLO checks. Step 5: Execute DB backfill during low-traffic window and monitor drift checks. Step 6: After 2 full weeks at 100% with no regressions, remove adapter and feature-flag code and mark ticket Done.
rollback_plan: If error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds at any canary stage, immediately revert gateway config to reinstate aliases and roll back the runtime change via the deployment pipeline. Run hotfix to re-enable legacy adapter. Postmortem to follow. All rollbacks must be coordinated with support and comms.
comments: 2025-11-19: Asha Kumar - Created ticket after spike showed 47 unique alias patterns across customers (logs from 2025-10). Recommended canonical manifest approach.
2025-12-02: Liam Nguyen - Implemented initial manifest_v2 schema; awaiting security review for schema fields that reference IAM principals (security review flagged optional).
2025-12-10: Design review - PM and Design suggested adding human-readable 'deprecation_message' field in gateway 410 responses. Decided to include short message and link to migration doc.
2026-01-08: Engineering sync - rolled feature-flagged compatibility adapter to staging. Observed +0.03ms p50, +0.8ms p99 in staging under synthetic load. Moving to small internal canary next.
2026-01-25: External comms - Drafted Console banner and automated email to 1,120 customers listing migration steps and deadline (2026-03-01).

2026-02-10: Canary 10% completed - realtime dashboards show stable error rates. Noted two customers still sending v0 queryparam flags; reached out to solutions engineering. Set due_date to 2026-03-01.
2026-02-20: Liam Nguyen - Gateway PR merged to remove alias routes behind phased rollout. Preparing final DB backfill during maintenance window.
Post-deploy checklist: ensure SDK telemetry records legacy usage hits and escalate if >0.5% after 2 weeks.
risk: Medium. Risks include missed customers still relying on aliases, DB migration locking issues, and accidental routing holes causing 404 loops. Mitigations include thorough inventory, staggered canary, and a visible Console banner plus support runbook.
notes: Related: this work complements previous efforts to canonicalize rollout manifests and remove v0 transport (see ENG-41234).
We should consider a short-term router-side redirect (301) for high-value customers that can't update immediately, managed by Solutions Engineering.
Post-cleanup telemetry should include an event that verifies no legacy query params observed for 30 days before archival.
